Forward planning  
Variation No.1 and No.2 to the County Development Plan 2021 - 2027  
Variation No.1 and No.2 were on public display from 25th February 2026 to 27th March 
2026 (inclusive of both dates) where submissions were invited from members of the public 
and statutory bodies.  
A total of 15 no. submissions were received to Variation No.1 and 12no. submissions were 
received in response to Variation No.2.  A Chief Executive (CE) Report has been prepared 
and shared with the members of Laois County Council for each Variation on 21st April 
2026. Elected members will consider the recommendations of the reports on the 25th May 
2026. If approved, and there are no material amendments, variation no.1 and 2 will then 
come into effect on the same day. 
Variation No.3 to the County Development Plan 2021 - 2027  
Variation No.3 was on public display from 6th March 2026 to 10th April 2026 (both dates 
inclusive) where submissions were invited from members of the public and statutory 
bodies. 
 
A total of 73 no. valid submissions were received.  A CE Report was presented to elected 
members on 01st May 2026. Elected members will consider the recommendations of the 
report by 12th June 2026.  If approved, and there are no material amendments, variation 
no. 3 will then come into effect on the same day.

The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant has been expanded, with effect from 31st March, 2026, 
to support bringing more vacant and derelict properties into use as homes. This includes the 
provision of top-up amounts to existing grant levels where vacant former commercial/public use 
buildings are being converted in their entirety into two or more residential units. 
 
From 31st March 2026, the following grants are also available: 
 
Vacant Above the Shop Grant 
A grant of up to €135,000 is available for the conversion or refurbishment of vacant above shop 
space into residential units for occupation as a principal private residence and/or for residential 
units), subject to appropriate planning permission being in place.  Where one residential unit is 
being created in the vacant above the shop space a grant of up to €95,000 will be available, where 
two residential units are being created up to €115,000 is available and where three or more units 
are created up to €135,000 is available. 
 
The Grant applies to vacant ‘above the shop’ space in buildings in cities, towns and villages, where 
the building was built prior to 2008 and the space/existing residential unit(s) have been vacant for 
two years or more prior to application. The ground floor commercial space may be vacant or in use 
at time of application but must be remaining in commercial use.  
 
Expert Advice Grant 
An Expert Advice Grant is available for Vacant Above the Shop Conversions and Conversion of 
former commercial / public use buildings to residential units.  The Expert Advice Grant provides 
funding of up to €5,000 towards having an appropriately qualified professional provide expert 
advice to the owner of;  
  
• 
A building with a commercial element and vacant above the shop space who may avail of 
the Vacant Above the Shop Grant to convert / refurbish the vacant space into residential 
unit/s, with the commercial element remaining. 
• 
A former vacant commercial / public use building who may avail of the Vacant Property 
Refurbishment Grant Conversion of former Commercial Building / public use building to 
convert the entire building into more than one residential unit. 
 
Only one Expert Advice grant can be applied for per building.  Applications can only be made by 
named individuals who own the building for which the advice grant is being applied, or who are 
actively engaged in purchasing the building. Where there is more than one owner of the building, 
all owners must be included on the application form. The Expert Advice Grant is not currently 
available to registered companies, developers, undertakings etc.

National Student Enterprise Awards 2026 
Paddy Lynch & Tom McDonald from St Mary`s CBS, Portlaoise  won 1st place overall in the Junior 
Category and the Intellectual Property Awards in the Junior Category, at this year’s Student 
Enterprise Programme National Finals which took place in Mullingar on May 7th. 
 
Their student enterprise was called: ‘I CAN, which offers a bottle and can collection and recycling 
service.    ICAN a door-to-door collection service that helps people return their bottles and cans 
and receive their deposit money without the hassle also won the Junior Intellectual Property 
Award.    This is the 24th year of the Student Enterprise programme, which has seen more than 
500,000 students take part since its foundation.  This national competition is a key initiative to 
promote entrepreneurship in Irish second-level schools.    
The event was hosted by broadcasters Rick O’Shea and Ruth Scott, and they were joined during 
the ceremony by Alan Dillon, T.D., Minister of State for Employment, Small Business and Retail to 
announce the winners across the three main categories on the day.

outdoor recreation and encompassing three elements: 
i)                    Digital marketing campaign. 
ii)                  Creative destination content showcasing the region through photography.

STEM Engagement Officer 
STEM Engagement continued in March with various schools and stakeholders. A welcome

DreamBig – Preparing TYs for the future of technology 
 
Hosted in conjunction with the Advanced Technologies in Manufacturing (ATIM) Cluster, the local 
authorities of Laois, Longford, Offaly and Westmeath, and TUS Athlone.  TY students were 
immersed into active advanced manufacturing working environments with a variety of companies 
farm March 2nd to 6th.   In Laois, 18 students attended workshops and sessions with Aubren, CJ 
Sheeran, Kirby, Midlands Steel, IMR Mullingar, and TUS Dept of Engineering. Students learned 
about sustainability development goals in manufacturing and the jobs needed today and the near 
future in engineering, design, coding, robotics and science.  The Laois STEM Engagement Officer 
(Laois SEO) and Broadband Officer coordinated with the companies and the ATIM Cluster 
throughout the process leading up to and during the week. A final Showcase in TUS on the Friday 
brought all 4 counties’ efforts together in one closing ceremony.

Laois Youth Voices Heard in National Parliament 
Six young people from Laois Comhairle na nÓg travelled to Leinster House on Friday, May 
1st, to take part in Dáil na nÓg, Ireland’s National Youth Parliament. 
Local delegates Logan Smyth, Abbie Holmes, Kacie Constantinou, Chloe Kavanagh, Róisín 
Bhreathnach and Veniamin Sahaidac joined 170 young representatives from Comhairlí na 
nÓg across the country to debate the critical issue of education – one of the biggest 
concerns for young people in Ireland. 
Now in its 24th year, Dáil na nÓg gives young people a national platform to share their 
views and make recommendations on issues that affect their lives. Delegates are elected 
through their local youth councils or Comhairlí na nÓg, Laois playing a key role in 
preparing the county’s representatives for the day. 
In the lead-up to the event, the young people took part in workshops where they heard 
from the Convention on Education and selected the topics they felt most needed 
attention. Two key themes emerged for debate in Leinster House: the Irish language and 
continuous assessment in schools. 
Hosted in the Dáil Chamber by Ceann Comhairle Verona Murphy, the event saw 
delegates outline how these issues impact their school experience and what changes they 
believe are needed. Further discussions took place in committee rooms, and the 
recommendations agreed on the day will now be submitted directly to the Convention on 
Education for consideration.  Minister of State Emer Higgins also addressed the young 
parliamentarians, emphasising the importance of listening to young people’s insights on 
education policy.   
Laois Comhairle na nÓg coordinator, Rosemary Kunene, said the event showed just how 
vital it is to involve young people directly in decisions that affect their lives. “Seeing our 
Laois delegates contribute so confidently to national discussions on education proves the 
importance of genuine youth engagement,” she said.
